# OpenChrome v1.12.0

Source: https://github.com/shaun0927/openchrome/blob/main/docs/releases/v1.12.0.md

# OpenChrome v1.12.0

Release date: 2026-05-14

## Summary

v1.12.0 is the largest feature release in the v1.x line. It merges the
entire accumulated `develop` backlog into `main`:

```
v1.11.1  →  v1.12.0   (cumulative, this release)

  878 files changed
  +111,050 / -8,148 lines
  972 commits (237 first-parent)
  105 PRs merged
  ~30 new MCP tools           (default tools/list now returns 110 entries)
  2  new MCP resources         (openchrome://state, resource subscriptions)
  5  new CLI command families  (oc run / oc replay / oc playbook / oc doctor / oc vault)
  0  source files removed
  0  new mandatory runtime deps (argon2 remains the only native dep)
```

This release builds directly on the **portability-harness contract**
established in the v1.11 line (see [`v1.11.1.md`](v1.11.1.md) for the
canonical v1.10.x → v1.11 reference). Every principle from that contract
still holds: the core tier preserves the v1.10.x surface bit-identically,
the pilot tier stays opt-in behind `--pilot`, no outbound LLM call is
required by either tier, and `argon2` remains the only mandatory native
dependency.

What v1.12.0 adds, in one sentence: a **goal-level task harness**, a
**deterministic recovery/reflection runtime**, a **CLI that can drive the
MCP surface directly** (one-shot `oc run`, declarative `oc playbook`,
`oc doctor` diagnostics), a **Streamable HTTP daemon mode**, and roughly
thirty new fact-capturing MCP tools — all while keeping the
facts-versus-decisions split intact.

---

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@1.12.0
openchrome check        # verify the installed CLI and runtime wiring
openchrome doctor       # NEW in v1.12 — full environment diagnostics
```

Fresh install:

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@latest
openchrome check
openchrome info
```

No configuration changes are required to keep your existing v1.10.x /
v1.11.x experience. Every new subsystem is either additive (new tools,
new CLI commands) or opt-in (`--pilot`, `--http`, new env vars). A
v1.11.x `~/.claude/.mcp.json` works unchanged.

The pilot tier is still opt-in:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openchrome": {
      "command": "openchrome",
      "args": ["serve", "--pilot"]
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Breaking changes

**No source-code-level breaking changes for tool callers.** Every existing
tool keeps its name, input schema, and core return shape. The items below
are the **observable behavioral changes** a v1.11.x user can hit. Each one
has a migration path.

### 1. `read_page` / `find` output now carries action-affordance markers

DOM-mode `read_page` and `find` output prefix each element identifier with
a compact affordance marker:

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `#` | text input (`input[type=text]`, `textarea`, `contenteditable`, `role=textbox/searchbox`) |
| `@` | link (`<a>`, `role=link`) |
| `$` | button / control (`<button>`, `<select>`, `role=button/checkbox/radio/combobox/...`) |
| `%` | visual target (`<img>`, `<canvas>`, `<video>`, `<svg>`, `role=image`) |
| *(none)* | plain text / structural |

```
# [142]<input type="search" .../> ★
$ [156]<button type="submit"/>Search ★
@ [289]<a href="/home"/>Home ★
[352]<h1/>Welcome
```

The marker is **display metadata only** and is rendered *outside* the
canonical identifier. Pass the identifier itself (`142`, `node_142`, or
`ref_N`) to action tools exactly as before.

**Migration**: if a downstream parser matches the *start of the line*
with a regex like `^\[(\d+)\]`, update it to tolerate an optional
`[#@$%] ` prefix (e.g. `^(?:[#@$%] )?\[(\d+)\]`). Parsers that extract
the bracketed identifier anywhere in the line are unaffected.

### 2. Interactive elements may now show an inline `[hints]` segment

The interactive marker (`★`) in DOM-mode output can be followed by a
bracketed hint segment — `★ [hint]` — when the serializer has extra
affordance hints for that node. Parsers that assumed the marker is always
exactly ` ★` should treat everything after `★` up to end-of-line as
optional metadata.

### 3. Console capture is now bounded by default

`console_capture` retains console entries under two new hard caps:

| Env var | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCHROME_CONSOLE_BUFFER_MAX_LINES` | `1000` | max retained entries per capture session |
| `OPENCHROME_CONSOLE_BUFFER_MAX_BYTES` | `4194304` (4 MiB) | max aggregate byte size; oversized single entries become a truncated placeholder with `truncatedFrom` recording the original size |

The `1000`-line default matches the legacy `maxLogs` default, so most
callers see no change. **Migration**: if you relied on effectively
unbounded console retention on a high-log-volume page, raise
`OPENCHROME_CONSOLE_BUFFER_MAX_LINES` / `_MAX_BYTES` explicitly.

### 4. Large-output tools can return an output handle instead of inline content

`read_page`, the crawl tools, `network_capture_*`, `extract_data`, and
`oc_evidence_bundle` may now return a compact **output handle** rather
than dumping a very large payload inline. Redeem it with the new
`oc_output_fetch` tool, which supports `offset`/`limit` pagination.

**Migration**: if your client only ever read the inline text result,
add a fallback: when a result contains an output handle, call
`oc_output_fetch` to page through the full content. Small results are
still returned inline as before.

### 5. Tier 1 tool surface expanded

The default `tools/list` surface grew by roughly thirty tools — a
default (no `--pilot`) introspection now returns **110 tool entries**.
All additions are **additive** — no tool was removed or renamed.

**Migration**: if your MCP client or test harness pins an exact tool
count, refresh the expected value. If it enumerates tools by name, no
change is required.

### 6. Streamable HTTP transport + transport lifecycle policy

A Streamable HTTP transport landed alongside a formal **transport
lifecycle policy** (`docs/transport-lifecycle.md`). **No transport is
deprecated** — `stdio`, `http`, and `both` all remain stable with no
sunset date. The policy document only establishes the *rules* for future
deprecations (minimum 3 minor versions or 6 months overlap). The
boot-time deprecation warning described in that document is not emitted
yet.

---

## New MCP tools

Roughly thirty new tools register on the core tier (no flag) unless
marked **pilot**. All are deterministic fact-capture / fact-transform
tools — none performs LLM judgement, consistent with principle P4.

### Goal-level task harness

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_task_start` | Open a host-driven task envelope; optionally forward args to an underlying tool. |
| `oc_task_get` | Read a task envelope by `task_id`. |
| `oc_task_list` | List task envelopes, optionally filtered by creation time. |
| `oc_task_update` | Update a task envelope's phase or note. Does not execute browser actions. |
| `oc_task_wait` | Block until a task envelope reaches a terminal state. |
| `oc_task_cancel` | Cancel a task envelope by `task_id`. |
| `oc_task_finish` | Finish a task envelope as `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. |
| `task_run` | Start an opt-in goal-level `TaskRun` — tracks user goal, success criteria, progress summary, item progress, and evidence across many tool calls without changing existing browser tools. |

The task harness is a **bookkeeping layer**, not an orchestrator: it
records goal/criteria/progress facts; the host LLM still decides what to
do next (principle P1).

### Crawl

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `crawl_start` | Start an async crawl job from a seed URL. Returns a job id. |
| `crawl_status` | Poll a crawl job by id; supports cursor pagination over discovered pages. |
| `crawl_cancel` | Cancel a running crawl job by id. |

Crawl results are delivered through the output-handle mechanism and
support cache modes documented in `docs/harness/crawl-cache-modes.md`.

### Page observation & element resolution

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_observe` | Deterministic numbered list of actionable elements — collapses the `read_page → query_dom → inspect → interact` pattern into one call. |
| `oc_query` | Resolve a semantic element query into stable refs using local AX/DOM matching only (no AgentQL, no LLM provider). |
| `element_pick` | Start/cancel an in-page human element-picker overlay; returns selector + DOM + style + bounding-box facts. Env-gated; does not persist skills directly. |

### Evidence, diff & context portability

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_diff` | Compare two evidence-bundle ids or paths; returns deterministic DOM / screenshot-pHash / URL / console / network diff facts. |
| `oc_context_export` | Export a tab's `ContextEnvelope` with a SHA-256 integrity hash. |
| `oc_context_import` | Strict-replace import of a `ContextEnvelope`; verifies the integrity hash first and rejects on mismatch. |

### Network capture

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `network_capture_lite` | Passive recorder for request metadata + headers (no bodies). Actions: `start` / `stop` / `getLogs` / `clear`. |
| `network_capture_full` | Recorder including capped response bodies; bodies over `maxBodyBytes` are omitted with `reason="over_cap"`. |

### Performance & Web Vitals

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_performance_insights` | Capture a CDP performance trace and return named insights (`LCPBreakdown`, `DocumentLatency`, `RenderBlocking`, `CLSCulprits`, …) plus a trace handle. |
| `oc_performance_analyze` | Drill into one named insight from a captured trace; returns Markdown detail + an evidence handle. |
| `oc_vitals` | Read-only Web Vitals snapshot of the current page — no injected page scripts, no added dependencies. |

### Recovery & reflection

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_reflect` | Create / get / list / validate reflection artifacts over a run's trajectory. |
| `oc_pilot_run_with_recovery` | **Pilot.** Bounded deterministic recovery wrapper around one tool call under declared safe recipes. Requires `--pilot` + `OPENCHROME_CONTRACT_RUNTIME=1`. |
| `oc_skill_replay` | **Pilot.** Replay a recorded skill (steps + optional contract) against the active tab. Returns `PASS` / `STEP_FAIL` / `CONTRACT_FAIL` / … |

### Diagnostics & policy

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_doctor_report` | Read the most recent `openchrome doctor` diagnostic report from cache (does not trigger new checks). |
| `oc_progress_status` | Read-only diagnostics for whether the current session is progressing, stalling, or stuck. |
| `oc_devtools_url` | Return the Chrome DevTools inspector URL for the active page — paste into any local browser to attach live DevTools. |
| `oc_policy` | Inspect the deterministic safety policy: `action="matrix"` lists irreversible-action rules; `action="evaluate"` previews a policy decision for a tool/args context. |

### Output handling

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `oc_output_fetch` | Redeem an output handle from a large-output tool (`read_page`, crawl, `network_*`, `extract_data`, `oc_evidence_bundle`); supports `offset`/`limit` pagination. |
| `oc_normalize_action` | Validate and normalize a near-valid browser/computer action payload **without executing it**. |

---

## New MCP resources

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `openchrome://state` (live state) | Read-only snapshot of live session state. |
| Resource subscriptions | MCP `resources/subscribe` support so a client can be notified when a subscribed resource changes, instead of polling. |

These join the `openchrome://skill-graph/<domain>` resource shipped in
the v1.11 line.

---

## New CLI

The CLI can now drive the MCP surface directly — useful for shell
scripting, CI smoke tests, and debugging without an MCP host.

### `oc run` — one-shot tool execution

`oc run <tool> [--arg key=value ...] [--json]` spawns the same stdio MCP
server an MCP host would, performs the initialize handshake, validates
the tool name via `tools/list`, and sends one `tools/call`.

```bash
oc run navigate --arg url=https://example.com
oc run read_page --arg mode=dom --json
oc run oc_assert --arg contract=json:'{"type":"text","contains":"Example"}' --json
```

Arg grammar: `true`/`false` → boolean, `json:<value>` → parsed JSON,
everything else → string. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` tool `isError`, `2` CLI
usage error, `3` transport/server failure. `--reuse` connects to a
running Streamable HTTP daemon instead of spawning a child.

**Sugar commands**: common tools have positional aliases that call
`oc run` internally — `oc navigate URL`, `oc click REF`,
`oc form_input REF VALUE`, `oc javascript_tool CODE`, etc.

### `oc playbook` — declarative YAML scenario runner

`oc playbook run <file.yaml>` executes a declarative scenario where each
step maps to exactly one MCP tool call. The runner is a thin client, not
a new orchestration tier. Each step carries an inline **Outcome
Contract** assertion instead of an LLM judgement, so runs stay
deterministic.

```bash
oc playbook run scenario.yaml
oc playbook run scenario.yaml --reuse --json | jq '.summary'
oc playbook run scenario.yaml --vars url=https://iana.org --out report.md
```

Supports variable substitution, `--reuse` daemon connection, and
Markdown report output. See `docs/cli/playbook.md`.

### `oc replay`

Replays recorded artifacts (recording / codegen replay support) through
the same thin-client path.

### `oc doctor` — environment diagnostics

`oc doctor` runs a battery of independent environment checks and writes a
cached `DoctorReport` (readable later via the `oc_doctor_report` tool):

- Node version, disk space, home-directory writability
- Chrome binary presence, Chrome port reachability, orphan-Chrome processes
- macOS permissions, optional native deps, PID-lock and profile-lock state
- Local + remote network reachability

### `oc vault` — credential vault

`oc vault save|list|delete|rotate-key` manages an at-rest encrypted
credential store for use by automation flows. Keys can be rotated
independently.

---

## Subsystem highlights

### Deterministic recovery / reflection runtime

A new family of modules (`src/recovery/`, `src/reflection/`,
`src/trajectory/`, `src/failure/`, `src/run-harness/`) records *what
happened* during a run so the host can decide *what to do next*:

- **Trajectory ledger** — append-only record of tool calls, progress
  status, and evidence per run (`docs/recovery/trajectory-ledger.md`).
- **Reward scorer** — deterministic scoring of recovery attempts
  (`docs/recovery/reward-scorer.md`).
- **Failure taxonomy** — structured classification of plan failures
  (`docs/orchestration/plan-failure-taxonomy.md`).
- **Reflection strategy / task-critic loop / subgoal decomposition /
  task-drift ledger / locator-fallback** — reliability building blocks
  documented under `docs/reliability/`.
- **Recovery runtime** — pilot-tier bounded recovery wrapper exposed via
  `oc_pilot_run_with_recovery` (`docs/pilot/recovery-runtime.md`).

All of it is fact capture and deterministic scoring — no LLM judgement
inside the server (principle P4).

### Transport: Streamable HTTP daemon

OpenChrome ships a first-class HTTP daemon mode so multiple MCP clients
can share one browser process, the server can outlive its launching
process, and sidecars can poll `/health` and `/metrics` independently:

```bash
npx openchrome serve --http 3100 --auth-token <token> --idle-timeout 30m
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3100/health
```

Full walkthrough: `docs/getting-started/http-daemon.md`. Transport
stability rules: `docs/transport-lifecycle.md`.

### Extraction pipeline

- **Static-fetch waterfall** — cheap static fetch before falling back to
  a full browser render.
- **Fit-markdown** — token-efficient Markdown extraction
  (`docs/recipes/fit-markdown.md`).
- **Semantic extract / scoped structured extract** — semantic and scoped
  structured-data extraction modes.
- **Cursor pagination** — `read_page` markdown mode and crawl results
  both support stable cursor pagination (`docs/mcp/pagination.md`).
- **Async crawl jobs** — `crawl_start` / `crawl_status` / `crawl_cancel`
  with documented cache modes.

### Perception & vision

- **Semantic `read_page` mode** — semantic page representation tuned for
  agent consumption (`docs/perception/read-page-semantic.md`).
- **Action-affordance markers** — the `#`/`@`/`$`/`%` prefixes described
  in breaking change #1.
- **Vision accuracy improvements** and **visual grounding** benchmark
  guardrails (`docs/perception/ralph-visual-grounding.md`).
- **`verify`** perception verification surface (`docs/perception/verify.md`).

### Observability

- **Structured logging** — machine-parseable log records.
- **Trajectory bundles** + **visual trajectory** — exportable run
  evidence (`docs/observability/`).
- **Token metrics** — per-run token accounting.
- **Progress notifications** — MCP progress notifications during
  long-running tool calls.
- **Resource subscriptions** — push instead of poll for live resources.

### Security

- **Secrets masking** — credential redaction across logs/outputs.
- **Host allowlist** — restrict which hosts automation may touch.
- **Credential vault** — at-rest encrypted store with key rotation
  (`oc vault`).
- **Irreversible-action policy** — deterministic policy matrix
  inspectable via `oc_policy`
  (`docs/security/irreversible-action-policy.md`).

### CLI / harness tooling

- **Doctor CLI** with a dozen independent environment checks.
- **Harness certification** + **candidate evaluation** harnesses
  (`docs/harness/certification.md`, `docs/harness/candidate-evaluation.md`).
- **Episode-harness** and **visual-grounding** benchmarks plus the
  **WebVoyager** benchmark runner (`docs/benchmarks/`).
- **Capability map generator** — `npm run docs:capability-map`
  (`docs/agent/capability-map.md`).
- **Auto-connect** — smoother first-connection flow
  (`docs/auto-connect.md`).
- **Research recipes** — composable host-LLM-driven research workflows
  with runnable fixtures (`docs/recipes/`).

---

## Storage policy & dependency footprint

Unchanged from the v1.11 contract. All new storage layers (task
envelopes, trajectory ledger, recovery state, crawl cache, credential
vault) use JSON / JSONL files plus `proper-lockfile` via the existing
`src/utils/atomic-file.ts` helpers. `better-sqlite3` is still not
adopted. `argon2` remains the only mandatory native runtime dependency.

No source files were removed in this release; no runtime dependency was
added or removed.

---

## Reliability & security carried forward

All v1.10.x / v1.11.x hardening continues unchanged:

- HTTP transport fail-closed policy (unauthenticated boots rejected
  unless `allowUnauthenticatedHttp: true` is explicitly set)
- Dashboard REST authz with tenant ownership checks
- File upload root restriction with `realpath` symlink resolution
- Screenshot + vision capture payload guards
- Same-origin CORS bypass scheme matching + DNS-rebinding defense
- Pilot handoff AES-256-GCM persistence with ephemeral-key default

New hardening in v1.12.0:

- Stale CDP reconnect completions are invalidated by a connection
  generation counter — an async connect that resolves after a
  `forceReconnect` can no longer resurrect a stale browser handle.
- HTTP request-stream `close` is distinguished from `aborted`: a normal
  end-of-stream `close` is no longer mistaken for a client disconnect.
- Console capture is bounded by line and byte caps (breaking change #3).
- Secrets masking and host-allowlist enforcement added across the
  automation surface.

---

## Verification

- `npm install`: clean
- `npm run build`: clean (`tsconfig.cli.json` + `tsconfig.json`)
- `npm run lint:tier`: 0 violations (522 modules, 1241 dependencies cruised)
- Full Jest suite: passes on the merged `main`
- Merge `develop` → `main` resolved 5 conflicts (`package.json` scripts,
  `dom-serializer.ts` affordance+hints combination, three test files
  taking the develop-side implementation)

# OpenChrome v1.12.1

Source: https://github.com/shaun0927/openchrome/blob/main/docs/releases/v1.12.1.md

# OpenChrome v1.12.1

Release date: 2026-05-15

## Summary

v1.12.1 is a focused follow-up to [v1.12.0](v1.12.0.md). It merges the
accumulated `develop` backlog — the **Competitive Benchmark Suite**
(Epic #1254), **browser lanes**, and **opt-in codegen replay artifacts** —
into `main`:

```
v1.12.0  →  v1.12.1   (this release)

  66 files changed
  +5,210 / -45 lines
  ~24 PRs merged (#1252–#1275)
  5  new MCP tools             (default tools/list now returns 115 entries)
  1  new CI workflow           (cross-platform benchmark matrix)
  0  source files removed
  2  new devDependencies       (js-tiktoken, playwright — dev/test only)
  0  new mandatory runtime deps (argon2 remains the only native dep)
```

Everything in this release is **additive or test-only**. The runtime MCP
surface gains five tools; the rest of the change is a new `tests/benchmark/`
subsystem, a benchmark CI workflow, and a small set of opt-in server hooks.
No existing tool changed name, schema, or return shape. A v1.12.0
`~/.claude/.mcp.json` works unchanged.

The facts-versus-decisions split from the portability-harness contract still
holds: the benchmark suite is pure measurement code, the new tools are
deterministic fact capture, and no outbound LLM call is required by the
core tier.

---

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@1.12.1
openchrome check        # verify the installed CLI and runtime wiring
openchrome doctor       # full environment diagnostics
```

Fresh install:

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@latest
openchrome check
openchrome info
```

No configuration changes are required. Every new subsystem is either
additive (new tools, new CI workflow) or opt-in (codegen replay behind an
env flag).

---

## Breaking changes

**None at the source-code level.** Every existing tool keeps its name,
input schema, and return shape. The single observable change a v1.12.0
client can hit:

### Tier 1 tool surface expanded (110 → 115)

The default `tools/list` surface grew by five tools — a default (no
`--pilot`) introspection now returns **115 tool entries**. All additions
are **additive**; no tool was removed or renamed.

| New tool | Tier | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `oc_skill_export` | core | Export a recorded skill as a portable artifact. |
| `oc_lane_create` | core | Open a task-scoped browser lane (isolated tab group). |
| `oc_lane_list` | core | List active browser lanes. |
| `oc_lane_get` | core | Read a browser lane by id. |
| `oc_lane_close` | core | Close a browser lane and release its tabs. |

**Migration**: if your MCP client or test harness pins an exact tool
count, refresh the expected value to `115`. If it enumerates tools by
name, no change is required.

---

## What's new

### Competitive Benchmark Suite (Epic #1254)

A new `tests/benchmark/` subsystem establishes a reproducible, cross-library
benchmark harness. It is **measurement infrastructure** — it ships the
scoring cores, fixtures, runners, and competitor adapters, with real
published numbers landing in follow-up runs.

**Harness foundation (#1255)**

- Shared result envelope + JSON schema (`tests/benchmark/schemas/result.schema.json`)
  so every axis emits the same machine-checkable shape, with embedded
  environment and competitor version pins.
- Environment capture utility — records OS, Node version, git SHA, and
  (for LLM-driven axes) the pinned model id.
- Competitor adapters for **Playwright** and **Puppeteer**, plus an adapter
  index. The registry of pinned competitor versions lives in
  [`benchmark/COMPETITORS.md`](../../benchmark/COMPETITORS.md); hosted/paid
  services are intentionally out of scope (not reproducible on a local run).

**Scoring axes**

| Axis | Sub-issue | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| Token Efficiency | #1256 | Field retention + payload compression vs. a structured ground-truth spec. Uses the `cl100k_base` tokenizer via `js-tiktoken` — a real, deterministic, pure-JS BPE tokenizer applied uniformly across libraries. Rubric committed *before* measurement (`tests/benchmark/fixtures/token-efficiency/RUBRIC.md`). |
| Agent Task Success | #1257 | Goal-completion scoring core, plus an expanded WebVoyager task corpus (tasks 11–18) with structural validation. |
| Speed / Latency | #1258 | Single-action latency runner against a local static fixture server — no network variance. |
| Reliability & Fault Recovery | #1259 | Flaky rate, recovery rate, and cross-platform stability. Ships a library-agnostic fault-injection proxy, CDP-level fault injectors, and a cross-platform benchmark CI workflow. |
| Developer Experience | #1261 | DX scoring core — quantifies setup/ergonomics friction. |

**Fixtures**

- Local static fixture server for deterministic latency runs (#1258).
- Local login-wall app fixture for auth-flow benchmarks (#1260).
- Token-efficiency starter corpus — three structured archetypes
  (e-commerce, news, docs) establishing the baseline measurement path (#1256).

**CI**

- `.github/workflows/benchmark-reliability.yml` — a path-filtered workflow
  that runs the benchmark suites across **macOS / Linux / Windows** on
  Node 18 / 20 / 22. `fail-fast` is disabled so every matrix cell runs to
  completion: the cross-platform pass rate is itself a benchmark metric.

### Browser lanes (#1037)

Task-scoped **browser lanes** isolate the tabs a single task touches, so
parallel or sequential tasks don't step on each other's tab state. Exposed
through four new core tools — `oc_lane_create` / `oc_lane_list` /
`oc_lane_get` / `oc_lane_close` — backed by `src/core/browser-lanes.ts`.

### Opt-in codegen replay artifacts (#836)

When codegen capture is enabled, the server records each tool call into a
replay envelope and attaches it to the tool result under a `replay` key.
Recorded skills can be exported as portable artifacts via the new
`oc_skill_export` tool. Both are **opt-in** — with the feature flag off,
tool results are byte-identical to v1.12.0.

### Observability fixes

- `oc_skill_export` and the `oc_lane_*` tools are registered in the tool
  annotations map and surfaced in the live-state snapshot, so introspection
  and the dashboard stay consistent with the registered tool surface.

---

## Dependency footprint

Two new **devDependencies** only:

- `js-tiktoken` — pure-JS BPE tokenizer for the Token Efficiency axis. No
  native or wasm component; runs on every CI OS.
- `playwright` — required by the Playwright competitor adapter in the
  benchmark suite.

Neither is a runtime dependency of the MCP server. `argon2` remains the
only mandatory native runtime dependency. No runtime dependency was added
or removed; no source file was removed.

Two new npm scripts expose the benchmark runners: `bench:latency` and
`bench:tokens`.

---

## Reliability & security carried forward

All v1.10.x / v1.11.x / v1.12.0 hardening continues unchanged — HTTP
transport fail-closed policy, dashboard REST authz, file-upload root
restriction, screenshot/vision payload guards, same-origin CORS + DNS-rebind
defense, pilot handoff AES-256-GCM persistence, stale CDP reconnect
invalidation, console-capture line/byte caps, secrets masking, and
host-allowlist enforcement.

This release adds no new attack surface: the benchmark suite is test-only
code, and the five new tools are deterministic fact capture / lifecycle
management with no outbound network or LLM call.

---

## Verification

- `npm install`: clean (`package-lock.json` synced to 1.12.1)
- `npm run build`: clean (`tsconfig.cli.json` + `tsconfig.json`)
- Full Jest suite: passes on the merged `main`
- Merge `develop` → `main`: no conflicts (clean three-way merge)

---

## References

- v1.12.0 release notes: [`docs/releases/v1.12.0.md`](v1.12.0.md)
- v1.11 canonical reference: [`docs/releases/v1.11.1.md`](v1.11.1.md)
- Competitor version registry: [`benchmark/COMPETITORS.md`](../../benchmark/COMPETITORS.md)
- Token-efficiency rubric: `tests/benchmark/fixtures/token-efficiency/RUBRIC.md`
- Benchmark CI workflow: `.github/workflows/benchmark-reliability.yml`

# OpenChrome v1.12.2

Source: https://github.com/shaun0927/openchrome/blob/main/docs/releases/v1.12.2.md

# OpenChrome v1.12.2

Release date: 2026-05-15

## Summary

v1.12.2 is the benchmark-readiness release for the Competitive Benchmark
Suite. It takes the v1.12.1 benchmark foundation and completes the next
layer of measurement infrastructure: expanded competitor adapters, larger
token-efficiency and WebVoyager corpora, per-axis runners, cross-platform
bridge smoke coverage, unified report generation, and the Epic #1254 close
gate that distinguishes mock-only evidence from measured benchmark
envelopes.

```
v1.12.1  →  v1.12.2   (this release)

  233 files changed
  +15,701 / -675 lines
  20 benchmark follow-up PR commits integrated (#1277–#1297)
  2  additional benchmark CI workflows
  43 WebVoyager tasks added (18 → 61)
  50 token-efficiency fixture pages added (5 categories × 10 cases)
  3  additional competitor adapters/bridges expanded or added
  6  benchmark report sections wired into the unified report pipeline
  0  new mandatory runtime dependencies
```

This remains an additive release. The runtime MCP contract is unchanged:
no existing tool is removed, renamed, or given a breaking input/output
shape. The new code is concentrated in `tests/benchmark/`, `benchmark/`,
`scripts/bench/`, and benchmark GitHub Actions workflows. Benchmark live
runs that need external credentials or browser-driver setup are still
opt-in; default CI continues to exercise deterministic and mock-safe paths.

---

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@1.12.2
openchrome check
openchrome doctor
```

Fresh install:

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@latest
openchrome check
openchrome info
```

No configuration changes are required for existing v1.12.x users. If you
only consume the MCP server or CLI, this release should be a drop-in patch
upgrade. If you run the benchmark suite, review the new runners and report
sections below because several benchmark axes now expose richer measured
or mock-safe envelopes.

---

## Breaking changes

**None.** v1.12.2 does not introduce any source-level breaking changes for
MCP clients, CLI users, or existing benchmark consumers.

Observable notes:

- Benchmark report wording is stricter about mock-only, opt-in, and live
  evidence so release claims do not imply completed live measurements when
  only deterministic envelopes are available.
- `parallel-isolated.mjs` no longer presents the retired 15.3× compression
  estimate as a benchmark result. Historical estimated claims were removed
  in favor of explicit measured sections.
- New benchmark workflows and scripts may require optional local tools
  when you deliberately run live competitor lanes; default project install
  behavior is unchanged.

---

## Benchmark suite improvements

### Harness and competitor coverage

The harness now has broader competitor representation and bridge coverage:

- Added a Playwright MCP competitor adapter.
- Added a Crawlee competitor adapter.
- Added a Browser Use Python bridge adapter and a cross-platform bridge
  smoke workflow.
- Kept competitor metadata centralized so benchmark reports can attribute
  results by library, execution mode, and evidence type.

These additions make the suite ready to compare OpenChrome against
browser automation libraries without forcing every CI lane to run expensive
or credentialed live tasks.

### Token efficiency benchmark (#1256)

The token-efficiency axis was expanded from a small seed set into a larger
fixture corpus and competitor matrix:

- Added a 5×10 deterministic fixture corpus covering docs, ecommerce,
  news, search-results, and SPA-style pages.
- Added per-page ground-truth JSON fixtures.
- Added a competitor matrix runner for token-efficiency comparisons.
- Added a tokens-versus-retention scatter chart.
- Wired the token-efficiency results into the unified benchmark report as
  section **A**.

The suite is now suitable for repeatable local/CI measurement of extraction
retention versus token cost, while still separating deterministic fixture
coverage from any optional live extraction cells.

### Agent task success / WebVoyager benchmark (#1257)

The WebVoyager-style agent task axis now has a much larger corpus and more
explicit execution-mode modeling:

- Expanded the task corpus from 18 tasks to 61 tasks.
- Added native/passive execution-mode support.
- Added N-gate helper logic for dry-run and regression gating.
- Added a library matrix runner to compare benchmark libraries by mode.
- Added report section **B** and CI regression coverage for agent-success
  evidence.

The release does **not** claim that every real-LLM/live baseline has been
completed. Instead, the benchmark surface is now ready to run and record
those live baselines in a controlled, opt-in way.

### Speed and throughput benchmark (#1258)

The speed/throughput axis now has first-class runner and report support:

- Added a throughput runner with `--skip-live` support for CI-safe paths.
- Retired the old estimation path so generated reports prefer measured or
  explicitly labeled evidence.
- Added speed and throughput charts.
- Wired section **C** into the benchmark report.

This axis is now one of the most release-ready parts of the benchmark suite:
it can produce deterministic report artifacts while preserving optional
live lanes for fuller comparisons.

### Reliability and fault recovery benchmark (#1259)

Reliability coverage now includes both matrix-style recovery measurement
and long-run stability sampling:

- Added a reliability matrix runner.
- Added a long-run stability sampler.
- Added JSON result artifacts for reliability and long-run stability.
- Added cross-platform bridge-smoke coverage for Browser Use integration.

The generated artifacts make reliability work auditable, but long-running
live cells remain intentionally opt-in so normal CI is stable and cheap.

### Auth and real-world usability benchmark (#1260)

The auth/usability axis now has a runner and setup-cost script set:

- Added auth setup scripts for OpenChrome, Playwright, Puppeteer, and
  Browser Use.
- Added LOC/setup-cost measurement helpers.
- Added an auth runner and `auth-usability.json` result artifact.

This prepares the suite to measure logged-in workflow setup friction. Live
logged-in smoke coverage still depends on the runner environment and is not
silently enabled by default.

### Developer experience benchmark (#1261)

Developer-experience reporting now has dual chart support and a benchmark
report section:

- Added DX scripts for common navigation/form-fill tasks across OpenChrome,
  Playwright, and Puppeteer.
- Added schema-completeness and actionability rubrics.
- Added DX chart generation for framework and MCP-oriented views.
- Wired DX evidence into the unified report as section **F**.

The current matrix is ready for measurement and review, while the report
continues to identify which task/library cells are measured versus queued.

### Unified benchmark reporting and Epic #1254 close gate

The unified report pipeline now assembles the per-axis outputs into
`benchmark/results/BENCHMARK-REPORT.md`. The Epic status document also
records a stricter close gate: Epic #1254 should close only after each
benchmark axis has produced a measured, non-mock-only envelope or an
explicitly documented live-run exception.

That distinction matters for release quality. v1.12.2 makes the benchmark
suite runnable and auditable; it does not overstate pending live evidence as
completed production benchmark results.

---

New or expanded benchmark automation includes:

- `.github/workflows/benchmark-agent.yml`
- `.github/workflows/benchmark-browser-use.yml`
- cross-platform Browser Use bridge smoke checks
- benchmark report generation scripts under `benchmark/`
- helper scripts under `scripts/bench/`

The latest `develop` checks used for this release were green for both the
main CI and benchmark workflows before the release branch was prepared.

- Benchmark-only and developer-only dependencies remain isolated to test and
  measurement workflows.
- No MCP tool was removed or renamed.
- The default server/CLI upgrade path is unchanged from v1.12.1.

# OpenChrome v1.12.3

Source: https://github.com/shaun0927/openchrome/blob/main/docs/releases/v1.12.3.md

# OpenChrome v1.12.3

Release date: 2026-05-17

## Summary

v1.12.3 is the live-benchmark execution and publication-gate hardening
release. It takes the v1.12.2 competitive benchmark infrastructure and
adds the missing runtime seams needed to run real-world benchmark episodes
against live or recorded-real evidence without overstating mock/scaffold
results.

The release focuses on four outcomes:

1. live LLM/tool-use loops can be injected and measured;
2. native competitor task loops can be exercised for playwright-mcp and
   browser-use;
3. live Chrome/CDP benchmark execution can use managed Chrome endpoints
   consistently; and
4. generated benchmark reports now fail closed before making headline
   claims without live/recorded-real postcondition evidence.

```
v1.12.2  →  v1.12.3   (this release)

  10 PRs integrated (#1326, #1328–#1336)
  1  browser startup cleanup regression fixed
  3  live/native benchmark execution seams added
  1  live throughput executor added
  1  live token-extraction wiring path added
  1  episode fault-injection integration layer added
  1  recorded-real corpus validator added
  1  final headline report gate added
  0  npm publish performed by this release-prep step
```

This is still a patch release for the OpenChrome runtime API. No MCP tool is
removed or renamed, and existing CLI/server consumers do not need to change
configuration. The new behavior is concentrated in benchmark execution,
validation, and reporting paths.

---

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@1.12.3
openchrome check
openchrome doctor
```

Fresh install:

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@latest
openchrome check
openchrome info
```

If you only use OpenChrome as an MCP server or CLI, this should be a drop-in
patch upgrade from v1.12.2. If you run competitive benchmarks, review the new
live/recorded-real gates below before publishing results.

---

## Breaking changes

**None.** v1.12.3 does not introduce source-level breaking changes for MCP
clients, CLI users, or existing benchmark consumers.

Operational notes:

- Headline benchmark report generation is stricter. Diagnostic, scaffold,
  dry-run, and mock-only rows are still useful, but they cannot pass the new
  headline gate unless they include eligible live or recorded-real evidence.
- Live benchmark lanes remain opt-in and may require browser runtime setup,
  competitor packages, and API credentials.
- `npm publish` was intentionally not run as part of this preparation; publish
  from a separate trusted terminal/session.

---

## Runtime fix

### Startup blank-tab cleanup (#1326)

Managed headed Chrome launches can create a transient startup tab. v1.12.3
narrows cleanup so OpenChrome closes only startup-owned blank/new-tab pages and
preserves user-created tabs that appear concurrently in attach mode.

Why it matters:

- avoids closing unrelated user tabs in attach-mode sessions;
- keeps the startup cleanup behavior useful for managed launches; and
- adds regression coverage for concurrently created `chrome://newtab` pages.

---

## Live LLM and native competitor execution

### Injected OpenAI Responses tool-use loop (#1328)

The benchmark suite now has an injectable OpenAI Responses tool-use loop. It
normalizes function calls, dispatches them through an MCP adapter, preserves
reasoning/function-call context across tool turns, and keeps budget accounting
inside the benchmark harness.

Key details:

- client and adapter are injected, so CI can test the loop without paid API
  calls;
- live execution is gated by explicit environment checks;
- reasoning model output context is retained with function-call outputs; and
- tests cover dispatch, final text handling, and fail-closed live env checks.

### Live real-world episode runner seam (#1329)

Real-world task completion can now distinguish deterministic/scaffold runs from
live or recorded-real measurement. The runner preserves canonical task/library
identity, rejects empty or unknown task selections, and requires explicit
pinning/evidence before headline eligibility.

This keeps benchmark claims honest: dry or scaffold rows are still useful for
harness regression, but they do not become publishable competitive evidence by
accident.

### playwright-mcp native task loop (#1330)

A native task loop for `playwright-mcp` now performs tool discovery,
navigation, snapshot collection, and postcondition checking through the native
MCP tool surface.

The implementation intentionally stays small: it does not introduce a new agent
framework, and it accepts both array and iterable/set-style tool discovery so it
can work with existing stdio MCP clients.

### browser-use native task bridge loop (#1331)

The browser-use path now has a native task bridge loop with explicit lifecycle,
timeout, and failure classification.

Improvements include:

- shared transport startup handling;
- unique bridge request IDs;
- timeout results reported as timeouts instead of generic failures;
- default native timeout aligned with the bridge transport timeout; and
- Python bridge syntax coverage through `py_compile`.

---

## Live benchmark measurement paths

### Live token extractor wiring (#1332)

Token/field-retention measurement can now use live MCP payloads. The extractor
opens a tab, calls `read_page` in the selected mode, parses structured JSON or
OpenChrome serialized DOM snapshot entries, and closes the created tab in a
`finally` path.

This avoids two common benchmark mistakes:

- treating raw substring matches as structured extraction evidence; and
- assuming OpenChrome DOM snapshots are always nested HTML instead of
  serialized snapshot lines like `<tag .../>text`.

### Live throughput executor (#1333)

The throughput benchmark now has a live executor that can launch managed Chrome,
thread the exact CDP endpoint into competitor adapters, and configure
OpenChrome's live adapter with the same host/port.

Notable safeguards:

- Playwright, Puppeteer, and OpenChrome all receive the selected CDP endpoint;
- OpenChrome receives an explicit derived port and `CHROME_HOST`/`CHROME_PORT`
  environment;
- managed Chrome is closed on normal completion and benchmark failure; and
- CI-safe tests verify endpoint/port propagation without requiring a live
  browser.

### Episode fault-injection hooks (#1334)

Reliability testing can now inject controlled fault plans into real-world
episode execution. The hook layer validates plan shape, rejects null or invalid
plans, and records injected fault events as part of episode evidence.

This moves reliability work closer to the primary benchmark axis: fault recovery
can be measured inside task episodes rather than only in isolated synthetic
micro-cells.

---

## Recorded-real evidence and publication gates

### Recorded corpus validator (#1335)

Recorded-real corpora now have a validator for publication readiness. It checks
manifest structure, competitor version pins, LLM settings, runtime metadata,
artifact references, postcondition evidence, and secret-like payloads.

The validator is intentionally deterministic and local. It does not require an
external scanner, but it catches common publication blockers:

- missing or malformed manifest fields;
- unsupported competitor version provenance;
- unpinned recorded libraries;
- missing final postcondition evidence;
- malformed artifact references;
- invalid failure categories; and
- likely secrets such as `sk-*`, Anthropic/OpenAI project keys, AWS access keys,
  and credential-shaped bearer tokens.

False-positive risk was reduced for benign prose such as “secret menu” or
“bearer authentication”.

### Headline report eligibility gate (#1336)

The final benchmark report path now includes a headline gate. Report generators
can require that every headline row is backed by eligible live, live-LLM, or
recorded-real measurement and final postcondition evidence.

This gate protects release claims by failing closed when:

- no headline-eligible rows exist;
- diagnostic rows are mixed into headline output;
- aggregate rows include runs without per-run postcondition evidence; or
- the generated real-world section still marks the headline gate as blocked.

A new `bench:realworld:headline` script records the intended release path for
headline real-world reports using a recorded-real corpus and
`--require-headline`.

---

## Benchmark direction and merge-readiness review

Before this release was prepared, the open benchmark PR stack was reviewed for
alignment with the repository direction and over-engineering risk. The accepted
shape is:

- benchmark logic stays under `tests/benchmark/` and `benchmark/`;
- default CI remains deterministic and credential-free;
- live or paid-provider paths are explicit and opt-in;
- publication claims require structured evidence; and
- runtime MCP compatibility is preserved.

The review found the merged work consistent with the v1.12 benchmark roadmap:
real-world task completion is the primary evidence axis, while token,
throughput, reliability, auth, and DX lanes remain supporting or diagnostic
unless tied to headline-eligible live/recorded-real task completion evidence.

## Benchmark readiness gate

### API-key-only readiness audit (#1337)

The benchmark readiness audit now distinguishes two questions that were easy to
conflate:

1. Is a benchmark axis headline-measurement-ready today?
2. Would providing only API keys/secrets make it headline-measurement-ready?

The answer for v1.12.4 is still **no** for every open benchmark issue. The new
readiness artifact reports:

```json
{
  "totalOpenBenchmarkIssues": 15,
  "headlineReady": 0,
  "apiKeyOnlyReady": 0,
  "nonKeyBlocked": 15,
  "apiKeyOnlyCanMeasureEveryOpenBenchmarkIssue": false
}
```

This means benchmark work can continue without overstating the current state:
API keys are necessary for some live LLM axes, but they are not sufficient until
non-key implementation blockers are cleared.

### New command

```bash
npm run bench:api-key-readiness
```

The command runs the benchmark readiness audit with `--api-key-only` and exits
non-zero until all non-key blockers are gone. Release workflows can use it as a
preflight gate before claiming that credentials are the only missing ingredient.

matrix and keeps #1310 as the open real-world headline eligibility gate.

# OpenChrome v1.12.5

Source: https://github.com/shaun0927/openchrome/blob/main/docs/releases/v1.12.5.md

# OpenChrome v1.12.5

Release date: 2026-05-25

## Summary

v1.12.5 is the first release cut after the OpenChrome direction was clarified in
SSOT issue #1359: **OpenChrome is a host-neutral MCP browser harness**. The
release keeps the package focused on real Chrome control, deterministic MCP
semantics, and portable evidence that can run under Codex, Claude Code, Hermes
Agent, OpenClaw, and other MCP-capable hosts without assuming a specific agent
runtime.

This patch integrates the full open PR stack that was pending after v1.12.4:

- startup Chrome lifecycle polish for real browser sessions;
- a state-graph and verified-memory pilot foundation;
- automatic skill/episode curation from successful task contracts;
- benchmark smoke and release-gate hardening that avoids overstated competitor
  claims;
- documentation/runbook updates for reproducible benchmark operation.

```
v1.12.4  ->  v1.12.5   (this release)

  12 PRs integrated (#1347 through #1358)
  1 host-neutral direction SSOT used as the merge gate (#1359)
  1 post-merge develop compatibility repair for lifecycle API reuse
  0 MCP tool removals
  0 npm publish performed by this release-prep step
```

---

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@1.12.5
openchrome check
openchrome doctor
```

Fresh install:

```bash
npm install -g openchrome-mcp@latest
openchrome check
openchrome info
```

If you use OpenChrome as an MCP server, CLI, or embedded harness, this is a
drop-in patch upgrade from v1.12.4. The new pilot/benchmark pieces are additive
and are gated behind their existing commands, flags, and test contracts.

---

## Breaking changes

**None.** v1.12.5 does not remove or rename MCP tools, transports, CLI commands,
or public configuration options.

Operational notes:

- The release does not publish npm from the release-prep automation. Maintainers
  should run `npm publish` separately after reviewing the tag and release notes.
- Pilot memory/curator behavior remains conservative and evidence-backed. It is
  intended to build portable host-neutral memory artifacts, not host-specific
  automation shortcuts.
- Benchmark additions improve reproducibility and release gating; they should not
  be read as a claim that every full live competitor benchmark is now published.

---

## Direction: host-neutral MCP browser harness

Issue #1359 was used as the final product-direction gate for this release. The
merged work supports the same core position:

1. **Real browser control first.** OpenChrome should remain a reliable MCP layer
   over actual Chrome/CDP behavior rather than becoming a synthetic agent runner.
2. **Host neutrality.** Features should work from different MCP hosts and coding
   agents without depending on Codex-specific, Claude-specific, or local
   orchestration assumptions.
3. **Evidence over claims.** Benchmarks, memory, and replay artifacts must be
   backed by explicit contracts, traces, and failure modes.
4. **Portable learning loops.** Pilot memory should accrete reusable skills from
   verified task outcomes while keeping deterministic schemas and clear
   provenance.

---

## Browser lifecycle and CDP reliability

### Reuse the startup blank tab on first `createPage()` (#1347)

When OpenChrome launches an isolated Chrome instance, Chrome commonly starts
with an initial blank/new-tab target. v1.12.5 teaches the first `createPage()`
path to reuse that startup blank target when it is safe to do so. This avoids an
extra blank tab in isolated launch flows while preserving attach-mode safety.

The behavior is guarded so it does **not** reuse a target when:

- OpenChrome attached to a user-owned Chrome instance;
- a target is already indexed;
- multiple untracked page candidates exist;
- the candidate target is a real site rather than a blank/new-tab URL;
- a non-default browser context is requested;
- resolving the startup target fails.

A post-merge compatibility repair keeps this behavior on the existing public
`CDPClient.getChromeLifecycleMode()` API instead of adding a second private
lifecycle method. This preserves the same lifecycle ownership contract used by
session cleanup and other CDP flows.

---

## Pilot state graph and verified memory foundation

### State graph hash anchor (#1348)

The pilot stack now has a minimal state-graph anchor over task transaction
records. This gives later memory and replay features a stable way to name page
state without coupling to a particular host process.

### DOM skeleton v2 hashing (#1353)

A second state hash mode folds a bounded DOM skeleton into the page-state hash
while keeping the original v1 hash byte-stable. The v2 path is bounded and has
fallback protection so hashing cannot expand without limits.

### Pilot bootstrap lifecycle (#1354)

Pilot startup and shutdown hooks are now idempotent. Embedded server tests and
host integrations can start/stop the server repeatedly without leaking pilot
subscriptions or timers.

### Automatic skill extraction from successful contracts (#1355)

Successful contract-backed task runs can now feed a conservative curator runner
that extracts reusable skill candidates. This is the first step toward verified
memory that is created from actual task evidence rather than free-form agent
summaries.

### Sidecar-backed curator stats and failed-run evidence (#1356)

Curator sidecars now expose stats and record `ok=false` outcomes. Failed-run
artifacts are hardened so negative evidence is available to future selection and
review logic.

### Auto-recall on task start (#1357)

Pilot auto-recall can promote curated skills when a new task starts. The recall
path is gated before pilot imports so non-pilot users do not pay unnecessary
startup or dependency costs.

### Deterministic SKILL.md body generation (#1358)

Curated journal slices can be rendered into deterministic `SKILL.md` bodies.
Sensitive body-builder arguments are redacted so generated memory artifacts do
not accidentally persist credentials or private payloads.

### Selector confidence accretion

The auto-memory layer can accrete selector confidence from task contracts. Exact
selector decay was corrected so repeated evidence adjusts confidence
predictably.

---

## Benchmark and release-gate hardening

v1.12.5 integrates the benchmark PR ladder that was planned after v1.12.4. The
focus is still safe measurement infrastructure and reproducibility, not inflated
headline claims.

### Contract and smoke hardening

- Stress thresholds for loaded runners are stabilized.
- Competitor smoke provenance is pinned and aligned with `COMPETITORS.md`.
- Empty-payload smoke rows are rejected.
- Operator CDP sharing is documented for repeatable smoke runs.

- Non-LLM benchmark axes are measured before live promotion.
- Real-world corpus contracts are locked before live episodes.
- Live LLM samples are gated before native execution.
- Native competitors are routed without OpenChrome fallback.
- Real-world tasks are stressed through final postconditions.
- Full benchmark release gates derive task counts from the configured suite and
  perform preflight checks.

### Operator runbook

The smoke runbook now documents the six-way competitor matrix and clarifies CDP
setup expectations for operators. This reduces the chance of accidentally
mixing mock/scaffold evidence with live benchmark evidence.
